description: Heap single and bulk user-property updates on the exact documented endpoint. Existing value, identity and batch checks are joined by advice for the reserved id property in every letter case. Other custom keys remain open. Account state and receiver acceptance require external evidence.

params.name: app_id
params.description: It is the Heap environment ID. Heap documents it as required.
params.fix_hint: Set app_id to the environment ID from Heap Projects.

params.name: identity
params.description: It is the known identity. Heap documents it as required. The server API cannot attach properties to an anonymous Heap user_id.
params.fix_hint: Send the same identity you use in Heap Identify.

params.name: properties
params.description: It is the trait object. Heap documents keys and values as strings or numbers, fewer than 1024 characters. The builtin Email property is the lowercase key email.
params.fix_hint: Send a properties object. Use the key email, lowercase, for Heap's builtin Email property.

params.name: property_value
params.description: The vendor documents `property_value` in the request contract.
The vendor documents `` in the request contract.

params.name: overlong_property_names
params.description: Property keys must have fewer than1024characters, counted afterJSONdecoding.

params.name: reserved_id_property
params.description: The official Add User Properties guide reserves all casings of id for internal variables. This advice applies to immediate property keys in single and bulk updates, not substrings, nested keys or account properties.
params.fix_hint: Rename this custom property. Keep the user identity in the top-level identity field.

params.name: method
params.description: This published ingestion operation uses HTTP POST.

params.name: content_type
params.description: Use a published request media type.

params.name: body
params.description: The request body is a JSON object.
